no-priors.name: No Priors
no-priors.bio: Podcast: The Changing Physics of Cybersecurity and Drug Development with OpenAI President Greg Brockman

html_en:
OpenAI's Greg Brockman made a striking claim this week: security spending should "vastly outstrip" software spending in the AI era — and a broader conversation about what AI can now genuinely discover, not just retrieve, is starting to take shape.

🔐 The New Physics of Security

In a wide-ranging appearance on No Priors, Greg Brockman made one of the bolder claims you'll hear from a frontier lab president this year:

"Cyber spend, security spend should actually vastly outstrip software spend. I think that people have not yet really internalized how much the physics around cybersecurity are going to change."

His reasoning: as software becomes near-free to produce, the bottleneck shifts to trustworthiness. You don't just want software — you want software that is reliable, secure, and believable. Aaron Levie echoed this from the enterprise trenches, noting that agent swarms capable of testing attack permutations, reading logs, and assessing data risk "only emerged in the past few months."

"Once you can get your data and infra into a better spot, at least you have a chance for agents to help you secure the environment... But everyone does need to do the hard work of getting the basics right at the start." — @levie

The optimistic read: agentic defenders can scale faster than human attackers. The pessimistic read: most enterprises can barely keep up with patching today.

🧮 AI That Actually Discovers

The math results Brockman references — roughly 400 significant open problems resolved — are worth pausing on. The question of whether AI can generate genuinely new knowledge, rather than recombine existing knowledge, has been the philosophical crux of many a dinner argument. Brockman thinks it's now settled:

"At this point, it's just impossible to deny, right? It is definitively, yes, possible... We are able to resolve these 100-year-old math problems."

But what's more interesting than the headline is what domain experts are finding when they dig into the proofs. Brockman describes mathematicians posting surprised reactions — "wait, why did they use that result over here?" — suggesting the AI isn't just brute-forcing solutions but finding unexpectedly elegant connections. He contrasts this favorably with the famously unsatisfying four-color theorem proof, which was essentially a machine-checked exhaustion of cases with no human insight to extract.

"The thing that I think we will see... is that there are beautiful insights within the work that these AIs have done." — Greg Brockman, No Priors

The implication for fields beyond math — biology, materials science, drug discovery — is that AI may not just accelerate research but actively contribute to it in ways that surprise even the experts reviewing the output.

🎨 AI Has Taste (And a Soothing Color Palette)

On a lighter note, the week's most viral AI moment may have been @thsottiaux's reminder that you can customize ChatGPT's web interface to make it, as they put it, "soothing." Over a thousand likes suggests there's a real appetite for AI tools that feel calm rather than clinical. Meanwhile, @petergyang shared an AI-generated piece with the simple caption: "This is beautiful. Who said AI doesn't have taste?"

On the more practical creative side, Peter Yang highlighted how HyperFrames is using Claude to replicate short-form video styles — upload a reference clip, describe what you want to change, and the model handles the structural translation. @jake11moran describes it simply:

"You can see where we're drawing inspiration from and apply a different font or different colors. It's still structurally the same idea."
Watch/Listen: Full AI video editing tutorial

📣 Consistency Beats the Launch

@zarazhangrui offered the week's most quietly useful piece of builder wisdom, in the context of AI content creation:

"Most people overestimate the importance of one huge launch and underestimate the power of just showing up every day on the timeline. Develop a system where you make a video every day > spending tens of thousands of dollars on a single launch video."

In a world where AI makes daily content production genuinely tractable for solo creators, this asymmetry matters more than ever. The moat isn't the viral moment — it's the habit.
html_zh:
AI正在重新书写人类知识的边界——从百年数学难题到企业网络安全，Greg Brockman的一席话提醒我们：这场变革的物理规律，大多数人还没真正理解。

🧮 数学只是开始：AI正在生产真正的新知识

本周最值得细读的一段对话，来自 No Priors 播客 对 Greg Brockman 的专访。OpenAI联合创始人兼总裁谈到了这一周令他最兴奋的事：AI解决了大量超过百年历史的数学难题。这不是小事。

"我们现在已经有能力大幅加速科学发现。关于AI究竟能否产生新知识，一直存在争议——但现在，这已经无可否认，答案是明确的：可以。"
——Greg Brockman，No Priors Podcast

他进一步说，这不是机器"吐出一个答案"那么简单，而是关于人与工具结合之后能达到什么高度：

"真正令人兴奋的是：一个装备了这些工具的人，能够实现之前完全无法想象的事情……几乎就像人类的杠杆率在急速攀升。"
——Greg Brockman

他还特别强调，AI产出的数学证明并非"无人能懂的机器输出"，而是包含了真正令领域专家惊讶的洞见——出人意料的推理路径，令人拍案的结果应用方式。这与四色定理那种"机器暴力枚举、毫无美感"的验证截然不同。

🔐 网络安全支出，终将超过软件本身

Brockman在同一期播客中抛出了一个更具争议性的预言：网络安全的支出，最终应该、也将会大幅超越软件本身的支出。这个论断呼应了 Aaron Levie 在推文中对企业安全现状的犀利描述。

"软件在某种意义上正变得越来越廉价。你不只是需要软件，你需要的是可靠的、安全的、你能信任的软件。我认为人们还没有真正内化：网络安全的物理规律即将发生多么剧烈的变化。"
——Greg Brockman，No Priors Podcast

Levie则从企业实战角度补充了这幅图景，描述了大多数大型企业当下面临的混乱现实：

"数据在大多数组织中高度碎片化，这意味着你根本不知道自己在任何时间点面临多大风险。某些系统权限开放过于宽泛，另一些则依赖'通过隐蔽实现安全'这种方式运营。"
——@levie

他也带来了一丝乐观：当基础数据和基础设施整理到位后，AI智能体可以真正发挥作用——扇形展开、调用安全工具、模拟攻击路径、分析日志。"这种能力在过去几个月才刚刚出现，在长时运行智能体和计算机控制成熟之前，完全不可能实现。"

🎬 AI视频创作：风格复制只需几分钟

在更贴近日常创作者的领域，@petergyang 分享了一个用 Claude 快速复制短视频风格的工作流，引发了不少关注。来自 @jake11moran 的原话是：

"我们把这个功能原生集成进了 @HyperFrames_ Studio。你只需上传或选取一个参考片段，然后用提示词描述你想改变什么。你可以看到我们从哪里汲取灵感，然后换一种字体或不同的配色——结构上还是同一个想法。"
——via @petergyang

配合 @zarazhangrui 的一条观察，这个话题有了更深的维度：

"大多数人高估了一次大型发布的重要性，却低估了每天坚持出现在时间线上的力量。建立一个每天做一个视频的系统，远胜于花几万美元做一个发布视频。"
——@zarazhangrui

✨ 界面美学：被忽视的AI产品战场

最后一个值得关注的小趋势，来自 @thsottiaux 的一条意外爆款推文——提醒用户ChatGPT网页版其实可以自定义外观、让界面更令人放松。这条推文收获超过1100个点赞，说明用户对AI工具的"感受层"有着被长期忽视的需求。

@thenanyu 则从产品预警角度指出了一个更深的问题：

"等到它出现在数据或用户研究访谈里，已经太晚了。伤害已经造成，声誉已经受损。"
——@thenanyu

界面细节、情感体验、早期信号的捕捉——这些"软"问题，正在成为AI产品竞争中越来越硬的壁垒。
